components.cost_effect: Each included cut adds its vector/scalar accumulation cost; all cuts share the single linear minimization over B.
components.goal: Use separation information without averaging infeasible query points into the solution.
components.key_estimate: The combined affine expression is a lower bound on F over X; Proposition 2.1 converts its minimum over B into the certificate guarantee.
components.name: Include nonproductive separating cuts
components.operation: All steps contribute to g and c; only productive steps contribute to A, xbar and best-point selection.
components.requires: Nonnegative weights, productive normalization and valid separation responses with the source sign convention.
transfer_checks: Recheck error terms for approximate cuts or approximate linear minimization.
Recheck existence and evaluation of the residual if B ceases to be compact.

content.family: Nonnegative weighted productive subgradients and nonproductive separating cuts

limitations.statement: The selected rule takes certificate weights and a valid productive protocol as inputs. It does not implement an underlying cutting-plane solver or an efficient rule for selecting weights.
Exact residual computation charges linear minimization over B separately. Approximate minimization requires a justified conservative error correction before certification.

performance_links.scope_note: Proposition 2.1 objective-gap guarantee for this given-weight postprocessing only; no bound on acquisition of a certificate with small residual.

variants.cost: No new Separation or First order Oracle calls when the full required protocol and productive values are already supplied. Separately charge one exact linear minimization over B. Direct accumulation costs O(τn) scalar arithmetic and O(τ) weight/value checks or comparisons, with O(n) accumulator storage in addition to input storage; this is an implementation operation count, not a source iteration-complexity theorem. Weight production and original protocol acquisition are separate resources and are not declared free.
implementation_details_ref: §2 equations (5)–(8), PDF pages 6–7; §1 PDF pages 2–3 definitions and computation discussion
variants.name: Given-weight postprocessing, equations (5)–(8)
variants.output: Return r, F_*, xbar and xbest. Both points lie in int X; no additional F evaluation at xbar is needed for the residual bound. Productive best-point selection uses stored values.
public_inputs: Dimension n; containing solid B with exact linear minimization; finite stored protocol (x^t,e_t,I,J); productive objective values; supplied weights ξ; optional accuracy target ε>0.
variants.query_and_update: Scan t=1,...,τ: accumulate g←g+ξ_te_t and c←c+ξ_t<e_t,x^t> for every step. For t∈I also accumulate A←A+ξ_tF(x^t), xbar←xbar+ξ_tx^t, and update best index to a productive query with smallest stored F value, resolving ties arbitrarily. Compute m=min_{x∈B}<g,x> with one linear minimization over B. Set residual r=c−m and F_*=A−r. These accumulations are a direct implementation of source equations (5)–(8); they do not specify how to generate search points or learn useful weights.
variants.requirements: X⊂R^n is a solid. F:X→R∪{+∞} is closed convex and finite on int X. At productive t, stored e_t is a subgradient and F(x^t) is available. At nonproductive t, stored e_t satisfies <e_t,y><<e_t,x^t> for every y∈int X. B⊃X is a solid with an available exact linear minimization procedure.
variants.state_and_initialization: Require τ≥1 and I={t:x^t∈int X} nonempty; J is its complement. Validate ξ_t≥0 for all t and Σ_{t∈I}ξ_t=1. Initialize g=0∈R^n, c=0, A=0, xbar=0∈R^n and best index unset.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: No iterative weight-selection method is included. Terminate after this finite scan and one linear minimization. For a supplied target ε>0, r≤ε certifies both returned feasible outputs via Proposition 2.1. If r>ε, the target is not certified by these weights; this does not imply either output actually has error above ε.

No unrestricted Oracle Complexity or weight-selection efficiency claim.

summary: Compute a residual, lower objective bound and feasible outputs from an existing protocol and supplied certificate; nonproductive cuts contribute only to the residual.
title: Given-weight accuracy-certificate postprocessing
use_when: Postprocess a valid stored protocol using supplied certificate weights and exact linear optimization over a containing solid.
